upsert.center: Aurelius Biotherapeutics
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on Aurelius current pilot-study page
upsert.contacts: Theresa Westfall, DVM — info@aureliusbio.com; (360) 961-3529 or (360) 734-0720
upsert.funding: Fully funded; Aurelius states there is no additional expense to owners for the trial.
upsert.notes: Initial pilot study combining an oncolytic peptide with adoptive T-cell immunotherapy for previously untreated stage 3–5(a) canine B-cell lymphoma. Almost all study treatment is performed in Bellingham, Washington; initial treatment requires about three days, followed by at least two later visits approximately a month afterward.

upsert.title: TriKE immunotherapy plus hypofractionated radiation for canine sarcoma
upsert.center: University of Minnesota College of Veterinary Medicine
upsert.status: Open and enrolling — confirmed on University of Minnesota current clinical-trial page
upsert.contacts: Amber Winter, CVT — 612-624-1352; contact through the official University of Minnesota study page
upsert.funding: Once enrolled, the study covers participation costs including blood/urine testing, imaging, radiation planning and treatment, TriKE immunotherapy and follow-up exams. Initial staging is also covered if performed at the Veterinary Medical Center.
upsert.notes: Dose-finding treatment study of TriKE immunotherapy with hypofractionated radiation in companion dogs with sarcoma. Local/regional lymph-node involvement may be accepted at investigator discretion; prior chemotherapy or radiation may be allowed after washout.

upsert.title: AKS-619d PD-L1-directed Ambifect immunotherapy for canine cancers
upsert.center: Purdue University Veterinary Hospital
upsert.status: Ongoing proof-of-concept study in client-owned dogs — owner-facing current enrollment route not independently confirmed
upsert.contacts: Purdue University Veterinary Hospital Oncology Service — owner prescreening through Purdue Oncology
upsert.funding: Confirm study-covered and owner-paid costs with Purdue Oncology.
upsert.notes: Independent Purdue proof-of-concept study of intramuscular AKS-619d, designed to induce antibodies targeting PD-L1. Public sponsor disclosures state client-owned dogs presenting to Purdue Oncology are screened for eligibility. The solid-tumor study excludes bladder cancer to avoid competing with the separate AKS-701d urothelial-carcinoma study. Kept out of patient matching until Purdue publishes or confirms a current owner enrollment route.
